174.t: Fish fries, home brew, lawn parties and tarpaulin dancing
174.s: Friday fish fries, backyard home brew, social clubs' dances, and dancing on rented tarpaulins in lawn parties.
174.q: Especially, you know, if you knew who was cooking it and you know they know how to cook. Yeah. So in them days, like I think I told you before, them people on a Friday, very few people in certain neighborhoods would cook. They'd say, well so and so got a fish Friday night. We'd get some gumbo,…

246.t: Fish fries and the red lantern outside the house
246.s: Glass and the interviewers describe fish fries and lawn parties, announced by a red lantern over the gate.
246.ch: Bands, halls and the Smoky Mary
246.q: Oh, well, fish fries, well they would be all over. Yeah. Yeah, all over. Sometimes we'd play at the Fry's on the Hall, there would be a big fish fry there.

430.t: Lawn parties and fish fries by day of week
430.s: Nothing special on weekdays; lawn parties were Sunday night and fish fries Saturday, with singing and clapping but no band.
430.q: No, not for the week, no, I mean, lawn parties, like they'd have lawn parties, well, that would always be on Sunday night. And, well, fish fries, you know, fish fries would always be on Saturday night, you see, you'd see the red lantern in there by the gate, you know, where you know that there was…

724.t: Food, beer and hours at the picnics
724.s: Describes the potato salad and ham, paper plates, keg beer, benches or chairs, and the band playing from about eleven till evening.
724.q: And straight chairs I guess or something like that. What kind of chairs? Straight chairs. It's on there straight chairs and the people would be sitting around there. Would they have the chairs in the middle of the floor? No, no chairs for the people. They would have to have them. Oh I see. People…

255.t: Saturday-night fish fries with guitar music
255.s: The family played at fish fries around the city, licensed by permit, where supper was charged and men treated the women.
255.q: A lot of times, all over the city they used to have fish fries. And they would have a white eye, a red light. And these guitar players, they'd make all these fish fries. And they would play, and people would be in there. And they would play up music, and they'd sing, and they'd dance by the guitar.…

1051.t: Surprise party and fish fries on Saturday nights
1051.s: Mrs. Henderson recalls a surprise party, and the couple recall fish fries and parties, with lanterns hung outside.
1051.ch: The Camellia band and home life
1051.q: Yes, I remember that. And then you could go from one place to the other and it wouldn't be too far. Especially with fish fries in there. Anywhere you would see a little lantern hanging outside, it was a fish fry.

752.t: Lakefront camps, 'pitch till you win' and beer kegs
752.s: How camps were rented, cooks prepared food, all-you-can-eat spreads and iced beer kegs; a milk aside and a note about a visitor arriving.
752.q: Yeah. Or people have them? Well, people, like you owned a big camp out there and they had a big dance floor and all. You rent that camp, see. I see. And sometimes they'd send your cook out there to cook your spaghetti and macadre and make your gumbo and stuff. See, like they had a big picnic like…

627.s: Cage describes quilting parties with coffee, tea cakes and singing, at which he sometimes played fiddle.
627.ch: Cage on work songs, church and social life
627.q: Oh my God's back the ice. Well don't worry. Yeah you might like it better with the ice. Okay thank you.

21.s: Description of lawn parties on vacant lots with canvas, lights and sandwiches, who promoted them, and the admission.
21.ch: Lawn parties, excursions and dance-hall work
21.q: Oh, yeah. They'd decorate all around the fences, lights. Different colored lights? Different colored lights. Oh, yeah? Yeah. They'd have all their expressions, all their barrels that'd be packed in the back, you know? That was lawn parties. Oh, dancing, sure. Do they have dance floors or just dance…

875.s: Howard and the interviewer discuss lawn parties and fish fries, who hires bands and which nights they were held.
875.q: Well the lawn parties, well it depends. Just like right across the street here. They have in the summertime, they have either fish fry or they have a party with music or you know. And that's the way that people rent your yard or foot-a-law and park. Oh yeah, that's right.

777.s: Williams played many picnics, which sell beer and sandwiches, but not fish fries.
777.q: They sell all this stuff. Beer, pop, no whiskey, no wine, sandwich and so on. It's like they give up fat. They sell all that kind of stuff.

292.t: Open house, fish fries and shrimp balls
292.s: House parties with piano and phonograph, Friday fish fries with music, and white shrimp and crab ball gatherings.
292.q: Yeah, we always had open house and we played piano. We'd have the radio, the phonograph going. Then after the phonograph left, we had the uh, the radio. The boys are cleaning the grass, I think.

831.t: No church music; lawn parties and their drinks and admission
831.s: He never played in church; lawn parties were in backyards with drinks and a small entry charge.
831.ch: Early bands and New Orleans musicians
831.q: Yeah, them was lawn parties. Did they sell drinks at lawn parties? Sure, did they sell drinks, for sure they sold drinks.

56.t: Prices and crowds at the fish fries in empty houses
56.s: He charged five cents a drink and held the dances in empty plantation houses at night for whole families.
56.q: Well, it mostly, it was in, in, in the room, you know. Oh, this was indoors. Yeah, because the entrance would wouldn't carry out.

849.t: Christmas party job at Mr. Commander's heated yard
849.s: He tells of his yearly contract at a house with heated yard and Christmas lights, and a priest leading a grand march.
849.ch: Starting out and leading a band
849.q: It's a beautiful place. All air conditioning in there. They got around about 500 some more tables. I know the Acme Insurance Company is fixing to give their Christmas party up there. I told them about a place. They asked me where they think they'd be able to get a place. And I would charge my band.…

825.t: Fish fries on Friday nights and a brother's gig
825.s: Dejan recalls younger brother Wilbert on drums at a fish fry, and how Friday fish fries worked with a red lantern outside and musicians sitting in.
825.ch: Drumming days and neighborhood life, 1919 onward
825.q: horn bro that hiding in the backyard in those days most everybody had a piano and once they had a piano you knew their band had to be there that's right and now out of ten times they could get musicians just come sit in for nothing you'd be passing that and you'd be coming off a job somewhere with…
